p8:main.derivation: Let H=A⁻¹+B⁻¹, h=A⁻¹a+B⁻¹b and k=aᵀA⁻¹a+bᵀB⁻¹b. Expanding both exponents gives xᵀHx-2hᵀx+k. Set C=H⁻¹ and c=Ch, so Hc=h. Then xᵀHx-2hᵀx+k=(x-c)ᵀH(x-c)+k-cᵀHc. The final two terms are independent of x, so normalizing the product leaves Gaussian N(c,C).
p8:main.checks: C is D×D and positive definite, c:D×1. Normalized density is (2π)^(-D/2)|C|^(-1/2) exp[-(x-c)ᵀC⁻¹(x-c)/2]. No commutativity of A and B was used.
p8:main.comparison_condition: General symmetric positive-definite precision sum and vector eta give C=(A^-1+B^-1)^-1 and c=C eta. Both complete-square derivations preserve matrix order and an x-independent constant, correctly retaining proportionality rather than equality.
